name: Leadership & governance
description: Digital health initiatives should be led through strong governance structures. Strengthening the governance of digital health at national and international levels through the creation of sustainable and robust governance structures, including regulatory frameworks, and building the capacity and skills needed for countries to promote, innovate and scale up digital health technologies.

name: Investment & operations
description: A robust strategy that integrates leadership, financial, organizational, human and technological resources and is used as the basis for a costed action plan. Identify and promote sustainable financing models in support of digital health development, implementation, integration and maintenance, including economic incentives, especially in artificial intelligence including machine learning.

name: Services & applications for scaling up
description: The adoption and use of digital health technologies in scaling up and strengthening health service delivery. Develop approaches that move health and well-being from reactive-care models to active community-based models, and reduce the burden of data collection from front-line workers by reorienting reporting-based tools into service delivery tools.

name: Integration & sustainability
description: Innovative integration of different digital technologies using shared services, with cross-sectoral partnerships at national level to align resources and investments and ensure the sustainability and growth of digital health. A national digital health strategy exists and is integrated in the national health strategy and actively used to guide development.

name: Standards & interoperability
description: Syntactic and semantic interoperability with WHO norms and standards as a cornerstone of health information to enable sharing of information in a connected world. Adopt open-source health data standards and aim for reusable systems and assets, including interoperability of health information systems both at national and international levels, ensuring data are of good and comparable quality.

name: Flexible digital infrastructure
description: A flexible digital infrastructure to support the digital transformation. The digital determinants of health, such as literacy in information and communication technologies and access to equipment, broadband and the internet, become more important as digital health becomes more prevalent, alongside issues related to legacy infrastructure, technology ownership and internet connectivity.

name: Adaptable health workforce
description: Build capacity and create a digitally-capable, adaptable health workforce. Capacity-building includes workforce assessment and instilling capabilities, attitudes and skills ranging from computer sciences, strategic planning, finance and management to health sciences and care delivery, and advancing digital health literacy among health workers and populations.

name: Legislation, ethics & compliance
description: Adopt legal and ethical frameworks, legislation, ethics policies and compliance, including regulatory frameworks and principles for the ethical use of health data in technologies such as artificial intelligence and big data analytics. Protect people against the misuse of information, malicious cyber activities, and inappropriate use of health data, safeguarding data security (confidentiality, integrity and availability) and privacy.

name: People-centred approach
description: Place people at the centre of digital health through appropriate health data ownership, adoption and use of digital health technologies, covering not only patients, families and communities but also health workers. Strengthen gender equality, health equity and accessibility for people with disabilities so that the introduction of digital health technologies does not aggravate inequality (do no harm).
